narrative:
The model estimates a 45% chance that you will leave your job, which is high enough for the company to deny your promotion as a precaution.

Three factors stood out most in this decision. First, your total years of experience across all jobs is only 1-5 years. Most employees the model expects to stay have similar short experience, so this pulled the prediction toward staying rather than leaving. Second, you have not received other job offers while working here. This is actually quite common—77% of employees predicted to stay also report no outside opportunities—yet the model still saw this as a factor that slightly increased the risk of you leaving. Third, you find it difficult to get involved in decisions or share opinions at work. This is uncommon; only 10% of employees expected to stay describe their involvement this way. This sense of limited voice pushed the prediction noticeably toward leaving.

Overall, your short overall experience and lack of external offers are working in your favor, but the feeling that your input is not welcomed is working against you and tipping the balance.

The organization should consider giving you clearer channels to contribute ideas and decisions. For your part, reflecting on whether this environment matches your long-term needs could help you decide if staying makes sense or if exploring new opportunities would be better.
